Hall Thruster

Radial B across the pole gap, axial E from the anode to the exit plane. Electrons are magnetized and drift azimuthally — the Hall current. Ions are not, and accelerate straight out.

View
Components
Outer shellAluminum, with the neutralizer housing and feed lines
Magnetic coreSoft-iron flux path: back plate, four return legs, pole pieces
Magnetic coilsCopper, wound on the legs and the center stem
Discharge channelBoron nitride ceramic annulus
AnodeGas distributor, fed by two opposed injectors
Cathode-neutralizerRefractory tube, tungsten insert

Illustrative geometry, modeled from the PPPL Hall Thruster Experiment concept figure. Not any real thruster's dimensions.
